accuracy.evidence: Checked against the PSHE Association programme of study KS4 (health and wellbeing: self-concept, media and body image) and DfE RSHE statutory guidance 2019. Research claims are attributed and kept to what the studies found: Kleemans et al. 2018 (teen girls and manipulated Instagram photos), Tiggemann et al. 2017 and Fardouly & Holland 2018 (disclaimer labels have little protective effect), Fardouly et al. 2015 (upward appearance comparison), Thai et al. 2023 RCT (one hour a day for three weeks improved appearance and weight esteem), Alleva et al. 2015 (functionality), Gilovich et al. 2000 (spotlight effect). No body weights or sizes are stated anywhere.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the beliefs that posted photos show how people really look (step 1 prediction, p2 selfie count), that a retouching label makes an image harmless (step 2 prediction, m2, challenge), that comparing with influencers is motivating (step 3 prediction 'Inspired and better'), that likes measure worth (step 4 thought 3, m8), that everyone notices your flaws (spotlight effect trap, m6) and that editing your own selfies protects you (habit sort, m7). The adult text names the label mistake and the just-ignore-it mistake.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbodyimg is the only lab that renders the same canvas photo twice and lets the learner stack six real-world edits (best-of-30 badge, warm light, low angle stretch with rippled floor, skin smoothing that removes texture dots, a warp that bends the door frame, and an eye-enlarging filter), then reuses that renderer for tap-the-clue hit regions. The highlight-reel drag sort and the three-option reframing step are new for Personal & Social labs; lab_distinct stayed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Every rule comes from the learner's move: toggling Reshape tool visibly bends the door frame and returns 'A warp tool pulls in the waist, and bends the background with it'; tapping the shirt in photo 1 returns 'Nothing was changed there. Look at the straight lines behind the person'; filing 'The best of 40 selfies' under not posted returns why it is exactly the kind of moment people post; choosing the filter-every-photo trap explains that selfie editing is linked to more body worry.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions are committed before the reveal: whether influencer photos are taken once or picked and edited, whether a retouching label stops viewers feeling worse (research says mostly no, which surprises most teens), and whether comparing with edited posts leaves people inspired or worse. Each is answered by the step that follows, and the task cannot complete until the prediction is made.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The challenge cycles six questions (upward comparison, warp clues, labels, protective habits, functionality, self-esteem) with rotated answer order, and every wrong option has its own explanation, such as 'That is downward comparison. Upward comparison tends to lower mood' and 'Heavy selfie editing is linked to more body worry, not less', followed by a Next one button.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text uses short sentences and everyday words (snap, shots, pores, mute, take breaks) with one defined term per paragraph (upward comparison, self-esteem), within the learner kid readability target. Adult text names programmes and studies in plain sentences within the adult target. Lab copy is one or two short sentences per message.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a fact, a clue or an action: how photos are made, what edits leave behind, what upward comparison does, and four concrete protective habits plus where to get help (trusted adult, GP, Beat). There is no generic praise, no be-yourself slogans, and no repeated sentences between kid text, adult text, lab and items.

mobile.evidence: On iPhone 13 portrait the canvas uses tall layout: the two photos sit side by side above six two-column edit buttons at least 46 px high, the clue photo fills the width, the reel bins split the screen in half with a large draggable card, and reframing options are full-width wrapped tiles. Every canvas action also has an HTML button below, so nothing needs precise dragging.

accessibility.evidence: Every action has a labelled HTML button (for example 'Reshape tool: turn on', 'Check the door frame', 'The best of 40 selfies: Usually posted'); the canvas aria-label and live region read each result aloud. Text is dark ink on white or tinted tiles in both themes, wrong states use red rings plus words, and axe passed in light and dark themes.
